record.original_question: For a reduced arithmetically Gorenstein set of points in projective space over a field of characteristic zero, is its h-vector always unimodal?

evidence.quote: Question 3.2. Is the h-vector of every reduced, arithmetically Gorenstein set of points unimodal (provided that the characteristic of the underlying field equals zero)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^n_k$ be a reduced, zero-dimensional subscheme (a finite set of distinct closed points) whose homogeneous coordinate ring $R/I_X$ (where $R = k[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ and $I_X$ is the saturated homogeneous ideal of $X$) is arithmetically Gorenstein, i.e., $R/I_X$ is a one-dimensional Cohen–Macaulay graded ring whose Artinian reduction is a Gorenstein local ring. Let $A = R/(I_X + (\ell))$ be an Artinian reduction by a general linear form $\ell$, and let $h = (h_0, h_1, \dots, h_s)$ with $h_i = \dim_k A_i$ be the $h$-vector of $X$ (so that $h_0 = 1$, $h_s \neq 0$, and $h_i = h_{s-i}$ by Gorensteinness).

Question: Is the $h$-vector $h$ necessarily unimodal? That is, does there always exist an index $j$ such that
$$h_0 \le h_1 \le \cdots \le h_j \ge h_{j+1} \ge \cdots \ge h_s\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the h-vector of every reduced arithmetically Gorenstein set of points in projective space (over a field of characteristic zero) is unimodal appears to be a well-known open problem. While non-unimodal Gorenstein h-vectors are known to exist for general Artinian Gorenstein algebras in codimension 5 and higher (Stanley, and later examples by Migliore–Zanello), it remains unknown whether such non-unimodal examples can be realized by reduced sets of points. Recent literature (e.g., Migliore–Nagel surveys and the Lefschetz Properties preparatory school notes) explicitly state this as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Reduced arithmetically Gorenstein schemes and simplicial polytopes with maximal Betti numbers
status_evidence.snippet: It would be extremely interesting to know if all arithmetically Gorenstein, reduced sets of points have (at least) the general Artinian reduction with WLP, because then we would have a complete description of the Hilbert functions of reduced, arithmetically Gorenstein sets of points.
status_evidence.claim: The full classification (which would imply unimodality) of h-vectors of reduced arithmetically Gorenstein sets of points is open.

status_evidence.title: Unimodal Gorenstein h-vectors without the Stanley–Iarrobino property
status_evidence.snippet: Non-unimodal Gorenstein h-vectors exist in codimension 5 and higher, but it is not known whether such examples can come from reduced sets of points.
status_evidence.claim: Non-unimodal Gorenstein h-vectors are not known to be realized by reduced point sets.

status_evidence.title: Lefschetz Properties Preparatory School Notes (Migliore–Favacchio)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses unimodality of Gorenstein h-vectors and lists the case of reduced points as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Unimodality of h-vectors of reduced AG point sets is listed as open in recent expository notes.
